label: Pliny reports Christians throughout the province of Pontus-Bithynia to Trajan

place.note: Provincial, not local: Pliny names no city. His letter reports Christians spread 'non civitates tantum sed vicos etiam atque agros' (not only towns but villages and countryside). Anchored at the Pontus region resource (857287); Bithynia, the other half of the province, is carried separately by lit-1peter-bithynia. Harnack (p. 187 n.) places the letter in the east of Bithynia-Pontus, near Amastris or Amasia, from the datelines of the surrounding letters.

date.note: Written during Pliny's governorship of Pontus-Bithynia; Harnack (p. 187) dates Ep. 10.96 to c. 111–113. The book-10 correspondence is a governor's dispatch sequence, so the range is fixed by the office, not by an internal date formula.

primary.cite: Pliny the Younger, Epistulae 10.96–97 (to and from Trajan, on the Christians)

secondary.cite: Harnack, Mission and Expansion, vol. 2, pp. 186–187

notes: Harnack calls this 'the most outstanding piece of evidence for the advance of Christian missions along the whole of the western coast' (p. 187). One apostate told Pliny he had left the faith more than twenty years before, pushing Christian presence in the province back toward c. 90. An official, hostile witness, which is why it is weighted as literary_contemporary rather than discounted.
